 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Michigan Football returns to action Saturday afternoon, traveling to Piscataway for a Halloween matchup against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights. With both teams struggling to find consistency this season, the Wolverines will look to reel things in and build some much-needed momentum heading into November.
 Michigan enters Saturday's contest with a 4-3 record (1-3 Big Ten) after suffering a frustrating 13-6 loss to Indiana last weekend. Despite holding the sixth-ranked Hoosiers to just 212 total yards, the Wolverines failed to find the end zone, continuing a troubling stretch of offensive performances.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Freshman quarterback Tommy Carr struggled in his first career start, completing 20-of-32 passes for 167 yards and an interception. Michigan's rushing attack also failed to establish itself, finishing with just 57 net yards on the ground.
 Fortunately for the Wolverines, Saturday presents an opportunity to get things moving in the right direction against a Rutgers defense that has struggled mightily this season. The Scarlet Knights enter at 2-5 overall (1-3 Big Ten), having lost three of their last four games. Rutgers has been particularly bad defensively, allowing approximately seven yards per play while ranking near the bottom of the country in several categories.
 Michigan's offense will also have an opportunity to capitalize on a Rutgers team that has struggled to protect the football. The Scarlet Knights have averaged more than two turnovers per game, including 11 interceptions through seven contests. Rutgers is also dealing with significant personnel concerns, as quarterback Dylan Lonergan has been ruled out, while standout wide receiver KJ Duff — who has recorded 774 receiving yards and nine touchdowns this season — is listed as questionable.
 However, the Wolverines have their own injury concerns to navigate, as offensive lineman Blake Frazier, defensive linemen Enow Etta, John Henry Daley and Dom Nichols, and safeties Rod Moore Jr. and Jordan Young were questionable on Friday's availability report.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement With Michigan needing two more victories to secure bowl eligibility, this matchup presents an opportunity the Wolverines can ill afford to squander.
 Game Info
 Teams: Michigan Wolverines (4-3, 1-3 Big Ten) at Rutgers Scarlet Knights (2-5, 1-3 Big Ten)
 Date: Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026
 Location: SHI Stadium — Piscataway, New Jersey
 Kickoff: 12:30 p.m. ET
 Television: Big Ten Network (BTN)
 Spread: Michigan -14 (subject to change)
 Today's question: Can Michigan's offense finally get back on track?
 After another frustrating offensive performance against Indiana, the pressure continues to mount on offensive coordinator Jason Beck and Michigan's offense. Rutgers presents one of the more favorable defensive matchups remaining on Michigan's schedule, but the Wolverines have repeatedly struggled to capitalize on opportunities against opponents this season.
 Will the Michigan offense finally put together a complete performance, or are the Wolverines headed for another unnecessarily stressful afternoon?
